'''Elon Lages Lima''' (July 9, 1929 – May 7, 2017)<ref>Circe Mary Silva da Silva, "[http://rmu.sbm.org.br/Conteudo/n33/n33_Entrevista.pdf Entrevista: Elon Lages Lima] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304105105/http://rmu.sbm.org.br/Conteudo/n33/n33_Entrevista.pdf |date=2016-03-04 }}", ''Revista Matemática Universitária'', Number 33, December 2002, pp. 97–120.</ref> was a Brazilian [[mathematician]] whose research concerned [[differential topology]], [[algebraic topology]], and [[differential geometry]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.abc.org.br/~elima |title=Brazilian Academy of Sciences: Elon Lages Lima |access-date=2015-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151124171901/http://www.abc.org.br/~elima |archive-date=2015-11-24 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Lima was an influential figure in the development of mathematics in Brazil.<ref>{{Cite web| url=http://rmu.sbm.org.br/Conteudo/n09_n10/n09_n10_Noticias02.pdf | title=Elon Lages Lima Professor Honoris Causa of the Federal University of Ceará | access-date=2016-03-27 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101125095412/http://www.rmu.sbm.org.br/Conteudo/n09_n10/n09_n10_Noticias02.pdf | archive-date=2010-11-25 | url-status=dead}}</ref>

Lima was professor emeritus at [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.impa.br/opencms/pt/pesquisa/pesquisa_pesquisadores/index.html |title=IMPA - Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada |access-date=2008-05-11 |archive-date=2008-04-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080417133959/http://www.impa.br/opencms/pt/pesquisa/pesquisa_pesquisadores/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> of which he was the director during three separate periods. Lima has been twice recipient of the [[Prêmio Jabuti]] from the ''[[Câmara Brasileira do Livro]]'', for his textbooks ''Espaços Métricos'' and ''Álgebra Linear'',<ref>{{Cite web| title=Matemática e Ensino, de Elon Lages Lima | language=es | trans-title=Mathematics and Teaching, by Elon Lages Lima | url=http://gazeta.spm.pt/getArtigo?gid=115 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140926173147/http://gazeta.spm.pt/getArtigo?gid=115 | archive-date=2014-09-26}}</ref> and of the Anísio Teixeira Prize from the Ministry of Education and Sports. His mathematical style was heavily influenced by [[Nicolas Bourbaki|Bourbaki]]'s.<ref>{{Cite web| url=http://rmu.sbm.org.br/Conteudo/n33/n33_Entrevista.pdf | title=Interview: Elon Lages Lima | access-date=2015-11-24 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304105105/http://rmu.sbm.org.br/Conteudo/n33/n33_Entrevista.pdf | archive-date=2016-03-04 | url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Biography==

He began his career as a high school teacher in [[Fortaleza, Brazil|Fortaleza]], [[Ceará]].  Lima graduated with a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[mathematics]] from the [[Universidade do Brasil]] (today [[UFRJ]]) in 1953. He obtained his [[PhD|doctorate]] in 1958 from the [[University of Chicago]] with [[Edwin Henry Spanier]] as advisor.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=6485|title=Elon Lages Lima}}</ref> He is a former [[Guggenheim Fellow]], and holds memberships in the ''[[Academia Brasileira de Ciências]]'' (Brazilian Academy of Sciences) and the [[TWAS|TWAS, the Academy of Sciences for the Developing World]]. He is a professor [[Honoris Causa]] of the [[Universidade Federal do Ceará]] and of the [[University of Brasília]], where he taught from 1964 to 1965.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nota do MAT/UnB - Falecimento do professor Elon Lages Lima |url=https://mat.unb.br/index.php/en-us/outras-noticias/282-nota-do-mat-unb-falecimento-do-professor-elon-lages-lima |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=mat.unb.br}}</ref> He was a member of the Upper Board of FAPERJ from 1987 to 1991. He was also a member of the National Board of Education.

He wrote over thirty books in [[mathematics]], some of which are intended for [[secondary school]] teachers. Between 1990 and 1995, he coordinated the IMPA-VITAE project, which held skills improvement courses for mathematics teachers in eleven cities from eight states throughout Brazil.

He received the ''grã-cruz'' ("Great Cross") of the ''[[Ordem Nacional do Mérito Científico]]'' ("National Order of Scientific Merit") of Brazil.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.abc.org.br/sjbic/curriculo.asp?consulta=elima |title=Elon Lages Lima – Membros da ONMC<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2007-10-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511075931/http://www.abc.org.br/sjbic/curriculo.asp?consulta=elima |archive-date=2008-05-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
*Lima, E. L. (1964). "[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF02566947 Common singularities of commuting vector fields on 2-manifolds]". ''[[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]]''. vol. 39, pp.&nbsp;97–110. 
*Lima, E. L. (1965). "[https://www.jstor.org/discover/1970383?sid=21105576010023&uid=4&uid=3737664&uid=2 Commuting vector fields on S3]". ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]''. vol. 81, pp.&nbsp;70–88. 
*[[Manfredo do Carmo|do Carmo, M.]] and Lima, E. L. (1969). "[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF01899010 Isometric immersions with semi-definite second quadratic forms]". ''[[Archiv der Mathematik]]'' vol. 20, pp.&nbsp;173–175. 
*Lima, E. L. (1987). "[https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265367242_Orientability_of_smooth_hypersurfaces_and_the_Jordan-Brouwer_separation_theorem Orientability of smooth hypersurfaces and the Jordan-Brouwer separation theorem]". ''[[Expositiones Mathematicae]]''. vol. 5, pp.&nbsp;283–286.
